page: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-200s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this server includes 32.0 GB of system memory, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a local 200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 10%. However, its multi-core CPU performance falls into the average category. Memory performance is robust, with large-block write bandwidth and PassMark memory scores ranking in the top 25%, though read-only bandwidth remains average. Tradeoffs are evident in multi-threaded decompression and database operations, both of which register in the bottom 25%. Static web serving throughput and prompt processing for small LLM models also perform in the lower tier, indicating potential bottlenecks under highly concurrent or I/O-heavy workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio (1:8) makes this instance a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute scaling. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource stealing. This hardware profile is best suited for memory-cached applications, moderate Redis deployments, single-threaded data processing tasks, and general-purpose workloads requiring a larger memory footprint relative to compute capacity.
